title: Bottled drinking water
description: At least 3 liters per person per day, enough for 3 days (9 liters per person).

title: Ready-to-eat dry food
description: Military rations, canned food, energy biscuits, and nutritious nuts.

title: Water purification tablets or a survival filter
description: Aquatabs or a portable filter for when bottled water runs out.

title: First aid kit
description: Roller bandages, sterile gauze, adhesive bandages, and povidone-iodine antiseptic.

title: Family prescription medicines
description: Blood pressure, heart, diabetes, and asthma medicines for at least 7–14 days.

title: Essential over-the-counter medicines
description: Paracetamol for fever, anti-diarrheal medicine, and oral rehydration salts.

title: Bright flashlight and spare batteries
description: A waterproof flashlight (IPX6) plus spare AA or AAA batteries.

title: Phone power bank (20,000 mAh or more)
description: Charge it to 100% and pack a universal charging cable.

title: Battery-powered FM/AM radio
description: Essential for rescue broadcasts when mobile networks and the internet are down.

title: Multi-tool and pliers
description: Open food cans, cut cord, and pry obstacles out of an escape route.

title: High-frequency rescue whistle
description: A whistle carries about three times farther than a shout and does not tire you out.

title: Lighter or waterproof matches
description: Start a fire for warmth, boil water, and send a smoke signal.

title: ID papers in a waterproof zip bag
description: Citizen ID, health insurance card, household booklet, and certified copies of birth certificates.

title: Small-denomination cash
description: ATMs and digital wallets fail completely during a widespread power outage.

title: Silver emergency blanket (Mylar)
description: Folds very small, reflects about 90% of body heat, and blocks wind and water.

title: Rain poncho and spare clothes
description: One long-sleeve outfit packed in a dry bag, plus a heavy rain poncho.

title: Certified life jacket
description: Required if your family lives in a low-lying area that can flood.

title: N95 mask or smoke respirator
description: Protects your airways from dust, ash, and disease after storms and floods.

title: Heavy work gloves
description: Protect your hands while clearing rusty metal, broken glass, and fallen trees.
